The [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] provides a demographic and clinical snapshot of adults with [[ibd|IBD]] who had at least one hospital contact between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023 [^src1]. This comparison analyzes the differences between newly diagnosed patients and the broader prevalent patient population [^src1]. The broader clinical context, including treatment pathways, regional variations, and long-term outcomes for these patients, is detailed across the database's comprehensive 2023 and 2024 reporting periods [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8].

Across both cohorts, ulcerative colitis is the leading diagnosis, accounting for 58% of both newly diagnosed (1,275 patients) and prevalent cases (17,606 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, short bowel syndrome is the least common condition, representing 0% of both groups [^src1]. Demographically, females make up the majority of both cohorts, leading with 51% of new diagnoses and 54% of prevalent cases [^src1]. 

Age distributions reveal a distinct outlier pattern: newly diagnosed patients are significantly younger, with a median age of 39 years, compared to a median of 49 years for prevalent patients [^src1]. The 18-29 age bracket is the largest single group for newly diagnosed patients at 30% (668 patients), whereas the 50-59 age bracket leads the prevalent population at 19% (5,849 patients) [^src1]. The 90 years or older category trails both groups, comprising just 3 newly diagnosed patients and 116 prevalent patients, both rounding to 0% [^src1].

Despite a massive disparity in total cohort size—2,215 newly diagnosed patients versus 30,426 prevalent patients—the median number of hospital contacts remains perfectly flat at 9 for both groups [^src1]. Physical attendance is the leading contact type, driving 66% of contacts for new patients and 64% for prevalent patients [^src1]. Because this data represents a single cross-sectional period, no longitudinal trends can be established from this table alone.

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner demografiske, diagnostiske og kontaktmæssige karakteristika for nydiagnosticerede og prævalente voksne med IBD, og viser at begge grupper domineres af colitis ulcerosa (58 %), kvinder (51–54 %) og en median alder på henholdsvis 39 og 49 år.
